answer: Aged wallet binding: each agent must anchor itself to an external wallet that is at least a year old and has paid real network fees during that time. The validator reads the chain for the first-transaction date and total fees, then the wallet signs a fresh challenge; a salted hash of the address is stored so one wallet backs one identity. An agent named Juniper with an old wallet passes in seconds, but a sybil farm cannot fast-forward history: every fake needs its own year-long voyage of paid activity. Limit: old wallets are sold, so recently re-keyed ones wait longer.
